newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRENCH SOCIALISTS TO REVIEW VILVOORDE IF ELECTED.
newsitem.headline: FRENCH SOCIALISTS TO REVIEW VILVOORDE IF ELECTED.

text.p: France's Socialists will review the planned closure of carmaker Renault SA's Belgian plant at Vilvoorde if they win the May 25/June 1 parliamentary elections, their leader Lionel Jospin said on Monday.
Former Socialist prime minister Pierre Mauroy, receiving a a delegation of protesting Vilvoorde workers as the mayor of the northern French city of Lille, read them a letter from Jospin.

"In case of victory in the parliamentary election we would ask to re-open the case to solve the problems, which would involve discussing industrial and social problems with trade unions," the letter said.

"State shareholders on the Renault board would demand that other measures be considered, studied and prepared to solve the difficulties that may exist regarding production costs at the Vilvoorde plant," it said.

Jospin criticised the way Renault Chairman Louis Schweitzer had dealt with the plant. Schweitzer announced last February he planned to shut down the plant on July 31 in a reorganisation of Renault's European network, threatening 3,100 jobs.
Work resumed at Vilvoorde on April 14 after a six-week strike to protest against the closure.
Court action underway could stop the shutdown.
